Family: Ariidae. Size: 62 cm. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.

Common names: Bronze catfish, Two-line sea catfish.
Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to the Indo-Malayan region, northern Australia, Queensland, and north to southern Japan. Type locality: Pondichéry ... Rangoon.

Inhabits coastal waters, from estuaries onto the continental shelf. Found mostly on mudflats; males incubate eggs in the mouth. Has sharp and venomous dorsal and pectoral spines that can inflict extremely painful injuries. Marine; freshwater and brackish. An important food fish.
Mainly opportunistic and carnivorous; feeding on sea urchins, crustaceans, fish, prawns, loose scales, and detritus.

Description: Dorsal spines (total): 1; Anal spines: 0; Anal soft rays: 17-21; Vertebrae: 53-58. Dorsomedian head groove bordered posteriorly by slightly raised frontals and forming a "V". Gill rakers usually absent on hind aspect of first 2 gill arches. Caudal fin lobes slender and tapered. Adipose fin short-based and located posteriorly.

Etymology: The genus name Netuma is a Tamil word that means "dance". The specific name bilineata refers to two lines (on the body).
